Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

estimandYLL 0.2.0

  • Add variance = "sandwich" to estimate_yll(). The model is fitted once, and intervals use the empirical sandwich variance of the pooled logistic score stacked with the standardization estimating equations (Zivich et al., 2025, arXiv:2504.13291). It accounts for both the hazard model and the target population’s covariate distribution. Spline knots are treated as fixed.
  • On yll_toy, sandwich standard errors were 0.97 to 1.02 times those of a 1,000-replicate bootstrap and of the spread over 500 simulated datasets. One call took 1 to 3 seconds; see notes/sandwich-validation.
  • With variance = "sandwich", survival_curves gains survival_reference_se and survival_exposed_se, and plot_survival() draws bands from them. Only normal-approximation intervals are available.
  • The variance is accumulated over groups of people, so memory use for predictions does not grow with the size of the target population.
  • The default remains variance = "bootstrap", so 0.1.0 results are reproduced unchanged. meta$variance records the method for every estimator.

estimandYLL 0.1.0

  • Archived on Zenodo as doi:10.5281/zenodo.23653506.

  • Replace the development API with estimate_yll(), two explicitly named comparator functions, and plot_yll() / plot_survival().

  • Require the baseline target population for the main estimator. Always return reference-minus-exposed restricted expected residual lifetime; remove policy interventions, display measures, and estimand-specific wrappers.

  • Keep the existing mortality models, annual pooled-logistic person-period expansion, individual conditioning, integration, and participant bootstrap.

  • Return one common five-element result with descriptive ERL and survival names, bootstrap estimates, and explicit failure records. Flag finite but impossible bootstrap lifetimes without silently dropping their values.

  • Keep normal and percentile intervals for the main estimator. All plotting functions return editable ggplot2 objects.

  • Validate incomplete data, duplicate IDs and invalid settings before fitting; preserve the caller’s random state and parallel/progress configuration.

  • Replace obsolete documentation with an English tutorial, interpretation and comparator articles, a migration guide, and a Japanese introduction.

  • Show public YLL examples at five-year starting-age intervals with 95% confidence intervals from 1,000 bootstrap replicates. Include the complete saved synthetic result and reproduction scripts, including a two-worker future check.
